newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia, Iran sign $109 mln shipbuilding deal.
newsitem.headline: Croatia, Iran sign $109 mln shipbuilding deal.

text.p: Croatia on Wednesday clenched a $109 million deal to build four ships for Iran, after an earlier agreement had been stalled for three years over disagreement on terms of payment, state news agency HINA reported.

"We have finally reached an agreement on the construction of four ships, that had been spoken of for quite a while," the outgoing Economy Minister Davor Stern, who co-signed the deal with Iranian Transport Minister Akbar Torkan told HINA.
Although the deal was first reached three years ago, it never became effective because Croatia refused Iran's condition that the payment be done in crude oil instead of money.

According to Stern, Croatia had worried that the influx of oil would not keep up with the pace of construction. "But now we have changed the contract and based it on money-for-goods principle", he added.
However, HINA said Iran was expected to acquire part of the funds by selling oil to Croatia's state-owned oil giant INA.

The construction of the first ship is to begin in three months and all four should be completed by the year 2000 in two shipyards in Split and Pula ports, HINA said. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
